figures.title: NAND output capacitance comparison
figures.caption: Capacitances are illustrative, not extraction results. Curves use the exact exponential; the stated estimate rounds ln(2) to 0.69.

figures.title: Setup and hold compete for skew
figures.caption: Same-edge flip-flops, independent setup/hold uncertainty budgets. Negative slack fails that specific check.
figures.alt: Setup and hold compete for skew. Positive capture-minus-launch skew buys setup time by spending hold margin; frequency reduction does not fix this hold deficit.
figures.takeaway: Positive capture-minus-launch skew buys setup time by spending hold margin; frequency reduction does not fix this hold deficit.

figures.title: Latch transparency and the closing deadline
figures.caption: An illustrative two-phase timing boundary. Downstream budgets must include actual arrival plus latch D-to-Q delay.
figures.alt: Latch transparency and the closing deadline. Borrowing is allowed only inside the capture window; it shifts the actual arrival downstream instead of creating free time.
figures.takeaway: Borrowing is allowed only inside the capture window; it shifts the actual arrival downstream instead of creating free time.

figures.title: SRAM bitline development and sense threshold
figures.caption: Constant current and fixed companion BL over a small swing. Chosen threshold represents offset/noise allowance, not a universal sense limit.
figures.alt: SRAM bitline development and sense threshold. Only one line moves in this model: do not double the capacitance, and do not enable sensing before the required differential develops.
figures.takeaway: Only one line moves in this model: do not double the capacitance, and do not enable sensing before the required differential develops.

figures.caption: Exact binomial bound under independent identical trials; correlation, repair and model bias need different treatment. This is not measured yield.

figures.title: Square-law CMOS VTC from current balance
figures.caption: Saturation uses I=β(VGS−VT)²(1+λVDS)/2. No subthreshold, DIBL or PDK fit; curves illustrate mechanism, not a modern process.
figures.alt: Square-law CMOS VTC from current balance. Changing relative pull-up strength moves the transfer curve; the operating output is where pull-up and pull-down currents balance.
figures.takeaway: Changing relative pull-up strength moves the transfer curve; the operating output is where pull-up and pull-down currents balance.
